prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of a Kimpurusha, a revered lion-headed human-bodied guardian of Kubera's lotus ponds in Hindu tradition.
ANATOMY: ONE sacred being with exactly ONE LION HEAD, TWO natural lion eyes, real thick mane and lion muzzle, HUMAN torso, exactly TWO HUMAN ARMS with human hands and TWO HUMAN LEGS with human feet. Opaque antique-gold and ivory layered cloth robe fully covers body, plain cloth sash, no crown or invented weapon. No paws, tail, wings, extra arms or Narasimha-specific symbols [kimpurushas-c01].
MOMENT: Step firmly across the stone rim of a lotus pond toward viewer, one human palm raised in commanding protective halt, other hand draws robe aside while stepping; lion head lowers with calm grave authority, mouth slightly open showing natural canines but no attack.
POWER: serving Kubera and guarding his lotus ponds; no magical attack or glowing body [kimpurushas-c03,kimpurushas-c07].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle among lotus leaves; imposing lion face, lifted HUMAN palm and robed torso fill square, normal humanoid scale through framing, no tiny human comparator.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one golden sunset shaft outlines living mane and opaque cloth, deep walnut pond shadows, ordinary disturbed water drops and floating lotus petals.
SURFACE: coarse living tawny mane, dark lion nose, weathered human palms, opaque woven robes, wet stone and textured lotus leaves.
SETTING: Kubera's lotus pond, pink and white living lotus flowers and dark water, no palace text or invented deity figures [kimpurushas-c07].
MOOD: reverential awe and formidable protective authority, never evil demon, cute mascot, ordinary man, statue or decorative portrait.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Kimpurushas
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

Seven Sangar checks pass.
